comment: Known expected state of verification commands (tempdoc 680 environment lane; contract tightened by tempdoc 872). Consumed by the known-state-hint hook (PreToolUse Bash): when a command matches an entry's `match` regexes, the claim is surfaced BEFORE the command runs so a session recognises a pre-existing red instead of re-deriving it via stash-and-verify. A PIN IS A DATED EXCEPTION, NOT A STEADY STATE: main being red is a defect, and the pin exists only so the defect is not rediscovered while it is being fixed. DISCIPLINE: every pin carries an exit — an `exitProbe` (a command; exit 0 means the pinned red is GONE; `slow:` prefix = only run with --slow) and/or a `reviewBy` date after which the pin must be re-affirmed with evidence or deleted. `node scripts/agent-analytics/expected-state-probe.mjs --gate` fails on a pin with no exit, past reviewBy, or whose exitProbe fired. A pin whose red is gone is a lie; delete it in the fixing PR. CI runs the --gate form WITHOUT --slow, so exitProbes run only locally; the CI check is shape + reviewBy, and a pin past its reviewBy turns CI red for every PR by design.

entries.claim: VduEligibilityPdfFixturesTest can be RED on THIS machine only (Tesseract/tessdata + Tika PDF env; @DisabledIfEnvironmentVariable CI=true, CI is green) — a local failure there is environmental, not your change.

scripts/agent-analytics/run-all-tests.mjs has several wall-clock-budgeted checks with thin margins on a checkout carrying 27 registered worktrees, so ordinary parallel-agent load pushes them over while each file passes in isolation. Three different files were observed failing this way in one session: world-state.test.mjs ('CLI smoke: completes in under 10s' -- world-state.mjs measures 8.0-9.0s bare), 861-w5-remove-worktree-teardown.test.mjs and 861-w5-agent-spawn-sweep.test.mjs. A run-all-tests failure is pre-existing IF the named file passes when run alone: re-run it with 'node <file>' before believing it. It is NOT the tempdoc-scan frontmatter read added in PR #604 -- collectClaims measures 195ms of the world-state run.
entries.evidence: Observed 2026-09-02 on worktree-resid-kernel: world-state.test at 12354ms then 8.0s/8.1s/9.0s across three consecutive bare runs of world-state.mjs; 861-w5-remove-worktree-teardown and 861-w5-agent-spawn-sweep each failed once in run-all-tests and passed 16/16 and 16/16 when run alone in the same minute. The budgets were set in tempdoc 743 P-J when the checkout carried far fewer worktrees, and these scanners' cost scales with worktree count. Deliberately carries NO exitProbe: the condition is load-dependent and an isolated re-run passes by construction, so a probe would report GONE against a live red -- the defect this PR fixed in three other pins. Second sighting the same day (tempdoc 886 PR 5b, worktree 886-ledger-1): 861-w5-agent-spawn-sweep.test.mjs ('CLI end-to-end: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID alone ... resolves the caller session') failed once STANDALONE and passed on the immediate retry with no code change, and an independent reviewer reproduced that standalone flake -- so for that file the condition is not only load-dependent; a second consecutive standalone failure is a real defect (owner: tempdoc 861 W5). 886 also widened known-state-hint's verification-command prefilter so `node scripts/agent-analytics/run-all-tests.mjs` / `*.test.mjs` can deliver this pin at all.

entries.claim: Match the SHAPE, not the name list: a worker-services test that fails as `java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException: <method>() timed out after 30 seconds` is CPU-starved, not broken. The 30s is the REPO-WIDE default (`junit.jupiter.execution.timeout.default` in build-logic/src/main/kotlin/conventions/JvmBaseConventionsPlugin.kt:117) — do not go looking for an @Timeout annotation on these classes and conclude the pin is wrong when you find none. They stand up a real Lucene index, the search executor or a real Tika extraction, so concurrent multi-agent Gradle starves them; a timeout in setUp() then cascades every case in the class. Observed across two families — search (FacetRegressionMatrixTest, RagContextOpsHybridCollectionScopeTest, SearchExecutorLegSetMatrixTest) and extraction (ContentExtractorTest, AdversarialCorpusIngestionTest, OfficeMarkerSearchabilityTest, PolicyDrivenTikaExtractorTest) — so treat a NEW name with the same shape as the same thing rather than as a new defect. IMPORTANT: starvation does not always surface as a JUnit TimeoutException. AdversarialCorpusIngestionTest fails as a plain AssertionFailedError reading `Malformed ZIP should map to PARSER_FAILED, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, or ... SUCCESS_EMPTY. Got: PARSER_TIMEOUT` — the assertion is real, but the value it saw is Tika's OWN timeout under the same starvation. So the test to apply is 'does the failure name a timeout ANYWHERE, including as an observed enum value', not 'is the exception a TimeoutException'. Re-run isolated before believing any of it; a failure here that names no timeout at all is yours. Same species as worker-core-onnx-longdoc-forensic-timeout.
entries.evidence: tempdoc 880 session f6617483 (2026-09-01): one full-suite run under concurrent multi-agent Gradle produced 9 failures across the three search classes, every one a 30s TimeoutException; re-run isolated on the same tree minutes later, BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 10s with zero failures. A separate full-suite run in the same session hit the four extraction classes with the identical TimeoutException-in-setUp shape. A third full-suite run produced the PARSER_TIMEOUT assertion variant in AdversarialCorpusIngestionTest, which likewise passed isolated (BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 14s) — that run is why the claim now tests for 'names a timeout anywhere' rather than for the exception type. modules/worker-services declares no dependency on app-agent or app-services (modules/worker-services/build.gradle.kts:12-26), and tempdoc 880's diff touches only app-agent, app-services, ui tests, docs and scripts — there is no path by which that change could reach these tests.

entries.claim: ReadinessTriggerCompositionTest waits up to 5000 ms for a readiness condition to clear and fails as `index.unavailable was still asserted after 5000ms` when the machine is saturated by concurrent multi-agent Gradle. It is a wall-clock wait on a background reconciliation, so the failure says the box was busy, not that the trigger regressed. Re-run isolated before believing it; a failure with a DIFFERENT message here is yours.
entries.evidence: tempdoc 880 session f6617483 (2026-09-01): failed in a full-suite run under concurrent load, passed isolated on the same tree in 11s.

entries.claim: A bare LOCAL full-kernel run reports 5 gates FAIL with kernel/input-missing (npm-audit, module-deps, dead-code, dead-code-jvm, config-surface). That is an UNBUILT REPORT, not a red: each finding names its producer command, and "node scripts/governance/run.mjs --produce-inputs --mode gate" builds them. Do not diagnose these as regressions from your change. Do not read it as "these gates are unenforced" either: CI builds all five inputs and evaluates the gates (Public-claims for the four node-produced ones, the platform-contracts unit-test lane for dead-code-jvm), so a regression IS caught on the PR that causes it -- just not by a bare local run.
entries.evidence: Reproduced 2026-09-02 on worktree-lane-B (base 6c3ba431); tempdoc 921 changed only the npm-audit gate's artifact name and source. The five missing paths are tmp/github-advisory-report.json, tmp/arch-preflight/module-deps.json, tmp/knip-report.json, tmp/dead-code-jvm-report.json and tmp/agent-evidence/_summaries/runtime-config-ownership-matrix.generated.json.

entries.claim: The wire gate reports contract-governance/buf-cli-missing until `npm install` has run in scripts/wire-contract/ (the buf CLI is a local devDependency, not committed). Environmental on a fresh worktree; not a contract regression. **But do not read that finding as a pass when your diff touches a .proto.** In the buf-cli-missing state the gate never inspects the protos at all, so it cannot see a breaking change — the environmental green masks the one check that matters. If the PR changes any .proto, run `npm install` in scripts/wire-contract/ FIRST and re-run the gate, and only then treat its result as evidence.
entries.evidence: Reproduced 2026-09-02 on worktree-lane-B (base 6c3ba431): the finding names scripts/wire-contract/node_modules/@bufbuild/buf-win32-x64/bin/buf.exe as absent. Claim amended 2026-09-02 during the #600 review: that PR added FailedJob.state (an additive field) to modules/ipc-common/src/main/proto/indexing.proto, and the reviewer had to install buf and re-run to get a real verdict (0 findings) — the pinned state alone would have been vacuous.
entries.exitProbe: slow: node scripts/governance/run.mjs --gate wire --mode gate --out tmp/wire-exit-probe.sarif && node -e "process.exit(require('fs').readFileSync('tmp/wire-exit-probe.sarif','utf8').includes('buf-cli-missing')?1:0)"
entries.exitProbeNote: 2026-09-02: the previous exit was `--gate wire --mode gate`, which exits 0 EVEN IN the pinned state — the gate reports buf-cli-missing as a finding but its verdict stays pass (fail-open on absent tooling, which is the very thing this pin warns about). It therefore reported GONE on the first --slow sweep that ran it, with buf verifiably absent from scripts/wire-contract/node_modules. The exit now asserts the FINDING is gone, not the gate's verdict, because the verdict was never the pinned state.

entries.claim: `jseval ui-a11y-gate` exits 2 (CAPTURE ERROR, not a violation) on the `security` and `security-light` steps: both time out waiting for `jf-settings-window dialog[open]`. The rest of the sweep is clean — 18 ok / 2 ERROR / 0 NEW violations. Read the exit code before the diff: exit 2 here means two steps could not be captured, NOT that accessibility regressed, so do not go hunting for a violation you introduced. Reproduced identically against main's own frontend, so it is pre-existing on main and not caused by your branch. A run that reports a NEW violation, or an ERROR on a step other than security / security-light, is yours.
entries.evidence: tempdoc 885 UL.9/UL.10 (2026-09-02): the same sweep run against two servers minutes apart — :5174 serving worktree-resid-product and :5173 serving unmodified main — produced byte-identical outcomes (18 ok / 2 ERROR / 0 new violations, exit 2) with both ERRORs naming the `jf-settings-window dialog[open]` selector (scripts/jseval/jseval/ui_selectors.py:57-68). 885:3596-3605 records the pass and says the next kernel-facing PR should pin it; this is that pin.
entries.exitProbeOmitted: No exitProbe, deliberately, and this is the honest form rather than a decoration. `ui-a11y-gate` drives a real browser against a SERVED frontend (`--ui-url`), so an unattended probe run by `expected-state-probe.mjs --slow` exits non-zero because nothing is listening — for the wrong reason. Exit 0 is what retires a pin, and this probe could never reach exit 0 whether the defect is fixed or not, which makes it an exit that cannot observe the pinned state — the defect `ui-web-envelopestream-heartbeat-flaky` records in its own exitProbeRetired, in the opposite direction. The real exit is lane R6's fix landing (worktree resid2-ui, wave-1 residue): when its PR merges, the fixing PR deletes this pin. reviewBy is the backstop if R6 does not land.
entries.fixOwner: wave-1 residue lane R6 (worktree resid2-ui) — the settings-dialog capture selector/wait in the ui-shot harness.

It passes green isolated (12/12) and green for the whole module (622/622) — a failure ONLY under the full run is pre-existing load contention, not a regression; re-run in isolation to confirm before treating it as yours.

Isolated re-run: `./gradlew.bat :modules:adapters-lucene:test --tests "*BatchUpdateIntegrationTest.concurrentRmwOnSameDocIdSerializedByCoordinator_402*"` — 12/12 green. Whole-module re-run: `./gradlew.bat :modules:adapters-lucene:test` — 622/622 green. Tempdoc 912 open item 11 records the shape and the (unconfirmed) timing-impact hypothesis against #612's CommitOps/RuntimeSession changes.
entries.exitProbeOmitted: No exitProbe: the test passes in isolation and for the whole module, so an unattended probe re-running it in isolation would report a false GONE — it would exit 0 whether or not the load-only flake is actually fixed, because isolation is exactly the condition under which it never reproduces. Retiring this pin needs either a targeted load-repro test or a full-suite run that no longer shows it, not a script this probe can run unattended.
